title: Workforce Planning and Budgeting
overview: Workforce planning is a critical HR process, interconnected with every other HR function, yet it is often executed inconsistently due to organizational and market complexities. This course explores the key drivers and performance indicators of workforce planning, presenting a practical model for forecasting employee demand and supply. Participants will learn how to address workforce gaps with controllable staffing strategies and gain hands-on experience with forecasting techniques commonly used in workforce planning. The course aims to equip participants with the tools to effectively manage workforce resources in alignment with organizational goals.
audience: This course is designed for recruitment and workforce planning managers, HR professionals, and strategy analysts with at least three years of experience in workforce planning, HR management, or business partnering.
methodology: The course incorporates a mix of interactive methods including brief lectures, group exercises, case studies, scenario analysis, and team presentations.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Define workforce planning within the broader context of HR management
Explain the connection between HR planning and the organization’s overall strategic goals
Understand the economic principles of demand and supply as they apply to the labor market
Apply forecasting tools to assess both the quantity and quality of human resource needs
Recognize the role of workforce planning in the staffing process
Analyze the external labor market's impact on workforce planning
Utilize budgeting techniques to support workforce planning initiatives
